title: Physical Fitness and Well-being
summary: Components of fitness, the benefits of regular activity, warm-up and cool-down, safe exercise, healthy eating and sleep, and mental well-being.

notes.text: Teenagers should be physically active for at least **60 minutes a day**. Regular exercise strengthens the heart, lungs, muscles and bones; helps control weight; improves sleep, concentration and mood; reduces stress; and lowers the risk of diseases such as diabetes, high blood pressure and heart disease.

rows: The heart and lungs supply oxygen to muscles over a long time
The force a muscle can produce
How long muscles can keep working without tiring
The range of movement at the joints
Moving quickly and changing direction easily

notes.title: Naming fitness components
notes.problem: Which component is mainly used in: (a) a long-distance run, (b) touching your toes, (c) lifting a heavy box?
steps: (a) Heart and lungs working for a long time: cardiovascular endurance.

items: **Warm-up** (5 to 10 minutes): light jogging and dynamic stretches raise your heart rate and body temperature and prepare muscles, which helps prevent injury.
**Main activity**: the game, sport or fitness programme.
**Cool-down** (5 to 10 minutes): walking and gentle static stretches let your heart rate return to normal and reduce stiffness.
Wear suitable clothes and shoes; drink water before, during and after exercise.
Use equipment correctly and play by the rules.
Stop if you feel pain or dizziness, and report injuries.

notes.label: First aid for sprains: RICE
notes.text: **R**est the injured part, apply **I**ce (wrapped in a cloth), **C**ompress with a bandage, and **E**levate the injury above the heart.

notes.title: Planning a session
steps: Warm-up: 5 minutes of light jogging and stretches.
Main activity: 20 minutes of a game or running.
Cool-down: 5 minutes of walking and stretching.

rows: Beans, eggs, fish, chicken, meat, soya
Vitamins, minerals and fibre for protection against disease

notes.text: Drink plenty of **water**; limit sugary drinks, fried food, chips and sweets. Eat breakfast: it gives energy and helps you concentrate at school.

items: Teenagers need about **8 to 10 hours** of sleep a night. Put screens away an hour before bed.
Mental well-being means coping with stress, enjoying life and having healthy relationships.
Look after your mind: talk about your feelings, spend time with friends and family, do activities you enjoy, spend time outdoors and ask for help when you need it.
